title: BA1/1197/2021 of SHUEB Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

paras.text:
HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
First Bail Application No. 1197 of 2021
Shueb ........Applicant

State of Uttarakhand ........Respondent
Present:-
Mr. Gaurav Singh, Advocate for the applicant.
Mr. V.K. Jemini, D.A.G. for the State.
First Bail Application No. 1705 of 2022
Afzaal ........Applicant

Present:-
Mr. Pankaj Kumar Sharma, Advocate for the applicant.
Mr. V.K. Jemini, D.A.G. for the State.
Hon'ble Ravindra Maithani, J. (Oral)
 Since both the bail applications arise from the
same FIR, therefore, they are being decided by this
common order.
2. Applicants Shueb and Afzaal are in judicial
custody in Case Crime No.270 of 2021, under Sections
489A, 489C, 489D and 34 IPC, Police Station Kotwali
Laksar, District- Haridwar. They have sought their release
on bail.

2
3. Heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the record.
4. According to the FIR, upon information, having
been received, on 18.03.2021, counterfeit currency notes
were recovered. From the possession of the applicant
Shueb, according to the case, Rs. 15,000/- currency
notes of different denominations were recovered. From the
possession of applicant Afzaal, according to the case, total
Rs. 12,000/- in different denominations were recovered.
5. Learned counsel for the applicant Shueb would
submit that mere recovery of counterfeit currency notes is
not an offence; it has to be shown that they were intended
to be used as genuine, which, it is argued, in the instant
case, has not been shown. On the question of recovery of
printer, scanner, at the behest of the applicant Shueb, it
is argued that merely recovery of some printer or scanner
does not prove that the applicant was possessing
instruments or materials for forging of counterfeit
currency notes; scanner and printer are available in every
household. It is also argued that it was found in the
house of Shareek also, who has already been granted bail
by the court below.

3
6. Learned counsel for the applicant Afzaal would
submit that mere possession of the counterfeit currency
notes is not an offence; no instruments were recovered at
his instance.
7. Learned State Counsel would submit that huge
recovery of counterfeit currency notes was made from the
possession of the applicants; at the instance of the
applicant Shueb, scanner, printer, some printed currency
notes and remaining pieces of papers have also been
recovered and the case of co-accused is quite different.
Hence, it is not a case of bail.
8. Mere possession of counterfeit currency notes
is not an offence, unless it has also been shown that
person possessing such currency notes had reason to
believe the same to be forged or counterfeit and further
that he intended that it may be used as genuine.
9. According to the police, from the applicant
Afzaal, counterfeit currency notes were recovered.
10. Without making much discussion, this Court is
of the view that the applicant Afzaal is entitled to be
granted bail.

4
11. In so far as the case of Shueb is concerned, it
is further case of the prosecution that on 19.03.2021, at
the instance of the applicant Shueb, from a room, which
he had taken on rent, printer, scanner, ink, paper
trimmer and other instruments were recovered. The police
also found from the drawer of the table some printed
counterfeit currency notes of different denominations.
12. On behalf of the applicant Shueb, it is argued
that the room was also in constructive possession of co-accused Shareek, who has been granted bail.
13. The recovery memo is on record, filed by the
State as Annexure-4 to the counter affidavit. According to
it, in fact, the applicant Shueb, at the relevant time had
told it to the police that he had taken the room on rent.
Though, he has stated that co-accused Shareek also
manufactures forged currency notes. Much discussion, at
this stage, is not expected. The court below granted bail
to the co-accused Shareek on the ground that nothing
was recovered from his possession. Applicant Shueb has
stated that he had taken the room of the room on rent. He
opened the door of the room by a key. It is not scanner or
printer, which were recovered. Some counterfeit currency
notes were also recovered from the drawer. There were

5
other instruments, there were some small pieces of paper,
which were residue of papers after printing notes.
14. Having considered, this Court is of the view
that there is no ground to enlarge the applicant Shueb on
bail.
15. The bail application of the applicant Shueb is
rejected.
16. Insofar as the bail application of the applicant
Afzaal is concerned, his bail application is allowed.
17. Let the applicant Afzaal be released on bail, on
his executing a personal bond and furnishing two reliable
sureties, each of the like amount, to the satisfaction of
court concerned.
 (Ravindra Maithani, J.)
 19.09.2022
Ravi Bisht
